    Yes, Pam Bondi was fired/removed from her position as U.S. Attorney General by President Donald Trump on April 2, 2026, rather than resigning voluntarily
    . Trump announced her departure on Truth Social, citing a transition to the private sector, following mounting frustration over her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files and pressure from congressional Republicans. 
    Key details regarding her departure include: 
    • Replacement: Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche was named acting attorney general.
    • Reasoning: Sources cited frustration with her leadership, particularly in the handling of Justice Department files related to Jeffrey Epstein, which drew sharp criticism and a congressional subpoena.
    • Background: Bondi was a loyalist who previously defended Trump during his first impeachment and was appointed as his second choice to lead the Justice Department. 
    Bondi stated she would be "working tirelessly" to transition to her successor and expressed that the role had been an "honour".

    As of March 2026,
    Joe Kent, the Director of the National Counterterrorism Center, resigned from the Trump administration in protest over the military offensive against Iran. Kent, a former Green Beret and ally, stated he could not in good conscience support the war, arguing that Iran did not pose an imminent threat, according to reports by NBC News and AP News. 
    • Who: Joe Kent, Director of the National Counterterrorism Center.
    • When: Announced resignation on Tuesday, March 17, 2026.
    • Why: Disagreement with the decision to go to war against Iran.
    • Context: Kent is the first high-profile official to step down in the second term over this policy, notes CNN and Facebook.
    • Investigation: Following his resignation, reports indicate the FBI is investigating allegations of leaking classified information, says NBC News.
